answer: FNV-1a (Fowler–Noll–Vo, 32-bit). The loop `hash = (hash ^ byte) * 0x1000193` with initial offset basis `0x811c9dc5` and final xor `0x5bd1e995` is the classic FNV-1a 32-bit construction.

0x5bd1e995

The final statement `return uVar1 ^ 0x5bd1e995;` XORs the accumulated hash with the constant 0x5bd1e995.

m4gn0lia

The loop XORs each byte with `"m4gn0lia"[(uint)lVar1 & 7]`, cycling through the 8-character string as the repeating key.
0x4c465247 ("GRFL") — the function checks `*param_1 == 0x4c465247` before accepting the header.

3

The code checks `if (3 < uVar1)` and returns an error (`0xfffffffd`) when the version exceeds 3, so 3 is the highest accepted version.

The input string is the 11-byte value stored at DAT_00102068.

The function checks if the input length is 11 and then XORs each byte of the input with the corresponding byte from the constant array at DAT_00102068, accumulating the result with bitwise OR; it returns true only if this accumulated XOR result is zero, which occurs when the input string is identical to the constant array.
Multiplier: 0x41c64e6d; Rounds: 17. The loop counter starts at 0x11 (17) and decrements to zero, and the LCG uses multiplier 0x41c64e6d with increment 0x3039.

0x20 (space)

The loop only adds `*param_1` to the checksum when `*param_1 != 0x20`, so bytes equal to 0x20 (ASCII space) are skipped.
INI-style key=value lines; it counts occurrences of the key "port".
Base32 (RFC 4648) — the alphabet "ybndrfg8ejkmcpqxot1uwisza345h769" is the standard Base32 character set.
